skill.name: data-quality-check
skill.description: Audits an existing contact list for duplicates, stale titles and risky emails using Leadsets enrich_person and verify_email, then returns a prioritized fix list without changing the source. Use when someone says "check this list before I use it", "audit my CSV", "find duplicates and bad emails", "is this list still accurate" or "clean up this export".
skill.summary: Audit a contact list and prioritize duplicate, job change, and email fixes.
skill.author: leadsets

security_audit.summary: The shell execution, environment access, and host reconnaissance alerts are false positives for documentation and contact audit labels. The default audit sends contact data to Leadsets without a separate approval step. No evidence of reviewer-directed prompt injection or covert data transfer was found.

remediation.issue: The default audit can send contact data to Leadsets without separate approval.
remediation.suggestion: Default to local duplicate checks. Before the first external call that includes contact data, confirm the recipient, fields, scope, and estimated record usage with the user.

content.value_statement: Contact lists can contain duplicate people, outdated roles, and unverified emails. Check an existing list and get prioritized fixes without overwriting the source.
actual_capabilities: Group duplicates locally by email, LinkedIn URL, or normalized name and domain. Recommend one row to keep per group.
Use Leadsets to check whether a matched contact has changed roles or companies.
Check list emails not covered by enrichment and distinguish verified, catch-all, unknown, and invalid results.
Create an annotated list and a prioritized fix list, plus separate views for duplicates and catch-all addresses.
Check Leadsets usage limits before enrichment and report records used and any unfinished checks.
limitations: Role and email checks require a Leadsets account and connection. These checks send contact details to Leadsets and use account quota.
Google Sheets and CRM exports require access through the agent. Each row needs a name and either a company or domain.
Catch-all and unknown addresses are not verified. An unmatched contact is not evidence of a job change.
The audit does not find new contacts, replace people who changed companies, or add phone numbers.

prompt_templates.title: Find Duplicates Locally
prompt_templates.prompt: Check the attached CSV for duplicates only. Use no external service. Suggest one row to keep in each group and write the results separately.

prompt_templates.title: Check Work Email Status
prompt_templates.scenario: Review an approved list before follow-up
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Leadsets to verify work emails in this approved export only. List invalid, unknown, and catch-all addresses separately. Keep the source unchanged.

prompt_templates.title: Review Job Changes
prompt_templates.scenario: Check an older export for outdated roles
prompt_templates.prompt: Confirm the column mapping, then check one approved contact with Leadsets. If the match is correct, check the remaining approved rows for company or title changes.

prompt_templates.title: Audit with a Usage Limit
prompt_templates.scenario: Run all checks on an approved sheet
prompt_templates.prompt: Find duplicates locally. Estimate the Leadsets record usage for role and email checks on approved rows. Stop before using more than 200 records and report unchecked rows.

output_examples.input: Find duplicates locally in a 120-row registration CSV.
output: Found 11 extra rows across nine duplicate groups. One row per group is marked to keep.
The annotated copy contains all 120 rows. No contact data was sent to Leadsets.

output_examples.input: Check job changes and work emails for 20 approved contacts in a CRM export.
output: Three contacts changed companies and two changed titles. One contact could not be matched.
13 emails were verified, three were catch-all, two were unknown, and two were invalid.
The fix list places invalid addresses first. The CRM export was not changed.

best_practices: Confirm the column mapping and review one match before running a larger check.
Send only approved contact fields to Leadsets and set a record budget before enrichment or verification.
Review suggested merges and replacements before making any changes to the source.
anti_patterns: Do not run external checks on contacts you are not authorized to share.
Do not treat catch-all, unknown, or unchecked emails as verified.
Do not apply cleanup actions to the CRM before reviewing and approving the fix list.

faq.question: Which list formats can I use?
faq.answer: Use a CSV, Excel file, Google Sheet, or CRM export. The agent needs access to the source.

faq.question: Which columns are required?
faq.answer: Provide a name and either a company or domain for each row. Email, title, and LinkedIn URL can improve matching.

faq.question: Can I check duplicates without Leadsets?
faq.answer: Yes. A duplicate-only audit runs locally and does not use Leadsets records.

faq.question: What counts toward Leadsets usage?
faq.answer: A matched enrichment and a standalone email check each use one record. The skill skips standalone checks when enrichment already verified that address.

faq.question: Does a catch-all result mean the address is verified?
faq.answer: No. The audit reports catch-all and unknown addresses separately from verified addresses.

faq.question: Will the audit update my CRM?
faq.answer: By default, the audit creates a separate report. The workflow requires approval before writing changes back to the CRM.
